title: Offices To Six Flats, Plus An Eleven-Bed HMO
desc: A former freight office and the six-bed HMO beside it, redeveloped as six apartments and an eleven-bedroom co-living scheme for professionals.

writeup.challenge: The scheme sits on Millbrook Road alongside a neighbouring property in the same ownership, and the two share a boundary and a party structure. The building had to reach a room count that works commercially while clearing the local authority's HMO standards on room sizes, communal amenity, kitchen provision and refuse storage, which is where schemes like this usually come unstuck.
writeup.approach: Eight bedrooms, all en suite, across ground and first floors, from 9 sqm up to 16.95 sqm. Two kitchens serve the house: an 18 sqm kitchen and dining space on the ground floor and a 9 sqm kitchen on the first, so no cluster of rooms is far from a kitchen. The existing conservatory came down and a new beam and block floor went in behind it. Every tea station is a wet area only, with no cooking facilities, which keeps the kitchen count honest against the standards. The external alterations were completed under permitted development rights, so the planning exposure sat where it could be controlled.
writeup.outcome: Documented to Building Regulations stage. The technical detail is where a large HMO is won or lost: acoustic bar on stud partitions between rooms, separating floors upgraded to Part E, a Category LD2 alarm system, and a fire strategy agreed with the fire consultant rather than assumed.

summary: A major redevelopment of two adjoining properties in Southampton, comprising a former freight office alongside an existing six-bedroom HMO, set within a substantial plot with large front driveways and extensive rear gardens.

The proposals involve the conversion of the former office into six new residential apartments, alongside the enlargement and complete reconfiguration of the adjoining HMO to create an 11-bedroom high-end co-living scheme for professionals. The co-living accommodation incorporates shared amenity space on every floor, while the apartments have been designed as high-quality homes for the local residential market.

Thistle Architecture has been involved throughout the entire project, from initial feasibility and pre-application consultation through to securing full planning permission, Stage 4 technical design and full interior design of both the apartments and co-living accommodation. Our involvement has continued into construction, providing Contract Administration and management of the works through to completion.

The project is currently under construction and is due to complete in December 2026, delivering a comprehensively designed mixed residential development comprising six new apartments and an 11-bedroom professionally focused co-living scheme.
